findings: The full-body hero shot clearly shows left-to-right robot progress with feet and body contained in frame.
The close-up clearly shows foot contact, particle displacement and leg geometry without visible clipping.
The final trail shot shows several distinct depressions and provides a readable consequence of the walk.
The hero/contact cut at 7.2 s and contact/trail cut at 10.2 s are clean; the closing transition begins at 13.0 s.
Opening, contact and closing typography remain within frame bounds. Closing title and supporting text are readable at native resolution.
Closing card accurately states 961,191 simulated grains, Apple M4 Pro and Experimental granular testbed; Solo12 attribution is present.
The final frame is entirely black as intended by the ending fade.
Previously inspected contact source frames 121 and 122 show no visible exposure, color or material discontinuity across the CPU-to-Metal render transition.

limitations: This is a technical and visual release check, not user acceptance; the user still needs to approve the final commercial.
Granules are uniform simulated spherical particles in an experimental shallow bed, not a calibrated real-sand model.
The crawl is controller-driven; this video does not demonstrate learned-policy inference or equivalence to NVIDIA simulation platforms.
Visual review used representative final frames, exact edit boundaries and prior sequential motion review; no subjective audio listening was performed.
evidence_scope: Review of the actual released MP4; does not claim bit-identical re-rendering from repackaged scripts.
